title: Tank drive
summary: One stick per side: your first driving code.

say.never: In **tank drive** each stick runs one side of the robot, just like a real tank has two tracks. The left stick runs the left wheels and the right stick runs the right wheels. Push both forward and the robot drives forward. Push one forward and pull the other back and it spins on the spot.
say.bit: Tank drive: one stick per side. Both forward drives; opposite sticks spin in place.

board.code:
left stick   ->  left side wheels
right stick  ->  right side wheels

both forward         ->  drives forward
one forward, one back ->  spins in place

say.never: Your code goes inside `teleopPeriodic()`, **between its curly braces `{` and `}`**. Anything between those braces runs over and over while you drive. Click on the empty line just under the comments, inside the braces. You'll type one line at a time, and the next three steps say what each one does.
say.bit: Click inside `teleopPeriodic()`, between its braces, on the empty line under the comments. You'll add three lines, one step each.

say.never: Type this line first. `double leftSpeed` makes a box named `leftSpeed` that holds a number with a decimal. `controller.getLeftY()` asks the gamepad how far the left stick is pushed up or down. The **minus sign** flips it, because pushing a stick *forward* gives a negative number and we want forward to be positive. Don't forget the `;` at the end. The lesson README has more on `double` and the sticks.
say.bit: Type `double leftSpeed = -controller.getLeftY();`. It stores the left stick position in a box, flipped so forward is positive.

marks.label: a box for the left side's speed
ask: how far is the left stick pushed?
flip it so forward is positive

waitFor.hint: type the left speed line inside the braces.

say.never: Press Enter for a new line and type this one. It does the same job for the other side: a box named `rightSpeed`, filled from the **right** stick with `controller.getRightY()`, flipped with a minus sign for the same reason. Two sides, two boxes.
say.bit: On a new line, type `double rightSpeed = -controller.getRightY();`. Same idea, for the right stick.

marks.label: a box for the right side's speed
ask: how far is the right stick pushed?
flip it so forward is positive

waitFor.hint: type the right speed line under the first.

steps.title: Line 3: send them to the motors

say.never: Last line. The two boxes only *hold* numbers, so nothing moves yet. `drive.setDutyCycles(leftSpeed, rightSpeed);` hands both numbers to the drivetrain, and the motors run at that power. The order matters: **left first, then right**. Each number goes from -1.0 (full backward) to 1.0 (full forward). Because it is inside `teleopPeriodic()`, it repeats about 50 times a second, so the robot follows your sticks.
say.bit: Type `drive.setDutyCycles(leftSpeed, rightSpeed);`. It sends both boxes to the motors, left first, then right.

say.never: Drive! **W** and **S** move the left side. The **up and down arrow keys** move the right side. Push one forward and pull the other back and the robot spins on the spot.
